answer: meadow records the attestation graph; zephyr samples independently rooted branches. kernel puts candidates whose support paths meet at one cut in the same admission series: head \(k\) needs \(2^{k-1}\) sampled branches to sign its judged work in one proof, and each branch is spent for that cut. Ten clones consume 1,023 distinct branch attestations; head ten needs 512 new communities. Parallel requests cannot reuse branches, and fresh wallets keep the cut. Growth means bribing exponentially many unrelated communities, while an independently rooted newcomer needs one attestation.
